purpose: This deliverable identifies the real humans who will decide the success, use, and payment of the software — including those nobody mentions in interviews because they operate behind the scenes. Without primary users who suffer the pain, there is no adoption; without a Sponsor who pays, there is no project; without mapping who can veto it, the project dies late and expensively.

steps.title: Silent Controllers and Influence Hierarchy
steps.summary: Map not just who is obvious, but who controls money, data, or deployment permission without interview mention, and rank everyone by real veto power.

substeps.title: Silent Controllers Search
substeps.objective: Find the invisible actors no interviewee mentioned but that the problem domain requires.
substeps.input: Primary User (Step 1) + business domain context (rural property rentals, deposit transfers).
substeps.raw_data:
- Money handler: Commercial banks processing deposit transfers and enforcing reversal rules.
- Regulation: National Tourism Registry (RNT) regulates rural lodging in Colombia.
- Production deployment: Internal operational decision, no external veto.

micro.title: Tracking questions
micro.objective: Execute tracking questions on money, regulation, and production deployment.

steps: Ask question 1: 'Who handles the data or money this solution will touch?'
Ask question 2: 'What legal or sector regulation applies to this type of operation?'
Ask question 3: 'Who approves the production deployment?'
List all uncovered entities as silent controller candidates.
how_to.table_columns: Tracking Question | Operational Reality / Domain Answer | Silent Controller Candidate
how_to.table_rules: One row per tracking question documenting candidate stakeholders.
restrictions: Minimum 1 tracking question must be answered.
Probe financial and regulatory domains even if not mentioned in problem interviews.
how_to.done_when: All tracking questions probed and candidates compiled.

micro.example:
| Tracking Question | Answer | Silent Controller Candidate |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Who handles the money this solution touches? | Deposits are transferred through commercial banks; banks establish processing cutoffs and reversal regulations. | Banking institution processing deposit transfers |
| What legal or sector regulations apply to this operation? | Rural tourism rentals in Colombia mandate formal registration with the National Tourism Registry (RNT). | National Tourism Registry (RNT) |
| Who approves production rollout? | No external technical entity; internal operational decision. | None additional |

substeps.title: Influence Hierarchy Assignment
substeps.objective: Assign each candidate exactly one type of influence in fixed exclusive order: Blocker > Sponsor > Validator > User.
substeps.input: Candidate roster from Sub-step 2.1 + Primary User (Step 1).
substeps.raw_data: Candidates: Banking institution, Laura Torres (CEO and founder), National Tourism Registry (RNT), Reservation Coordinator.

steps: Review the fixed influence hierarchy: Blocker > Sponsor > Validator > User.
Assign each candidate to their candidate role categories.
Document candidate classification options.
how_to.table_rules: One row per candidate outlining role possibilities.

| Reservation Coordinator | User | Executes daily reservations and calendar checks |

micro.title: Exclusivity rule application
micro.objective: Resolve multi-role conflicts by assigning the role with greater political/financial weight.

steps: Apply the exclusivity rule: if a stakeholder qualifies for multiple roles, assign the role with highest hierarchical weight.
Hierarchy rank: Blocker (highest) > Sponsor > Validator > User (lowest).
Assign exactly one final Influence type per stakeholder.
Verify no stakeholder holds multiple influence designations.
how_to.table_columns: Candidate | Potential Role(s) | Conflict Resolution / Rationale | Assigned Influence
how_to.table_rules: One row per stakeholder detailing exclusivity resolution.

substeps.title: Independent Blocker Flag
substeps.objective: Capture operational veto power even in actors of low hierarchical weight.

micro.title: Blocker flag evaluation
micro.objective: Apply the flag question: 'If this person refuses to cooperate, does the project die?'

steps: For every stakeholder, ask the independent veto question: 'If this person/entity refuses to cooperate, does the project die?'
Evaluate operational boycott or procedural refusal risk.
Assign Blocker Flag: YES or NO (with timeframe if conditional).
Confirm that operational users or external regulators can hold Blocker Flag YES regardless of their influence category.
how_to.table_columns: Candidate | Influence | Does project terminate if they refuse to cooperate? | Blocker Flag
how_to.table_rules: One row per stakeholder checking independent veto power.
restrictions: Blocker Flag is independent of Influence category.
Be realistic about user boycott and financial withdrawal.
how_to.done_when: Blocker flag assigned to all stakeholders.
